### **Job Description and Duties**


Are you an environmental scientist who is passionate about protecting California from harmful and toxic substances? Are you looking to work in a dynamic and fast paced setting? Do you enjoy challenges and opportunities that require you to push your skills and abilities to new levels? Then consider joining the Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC) Waste Evaluation and Recycling Unit’s team!  

**As an Environmental Scientist you will have the opportunity to:**
* Work in conjunction with Senior Environmental Scientists (Specialist) of the Waste Evaluation and Recycling Unit on the interpretation and application of the hazardous waste identification requirements and criteria, as well as the statutory and regulatory exclusions and exemptions available to different waste types and waste management practices including, but not limited to, recyclable materials;
* Develop responses to the inquiries from stakeholders for interpretation of the hazardous waste identification requirements and criteria, as well as the statutory and regulatory exclusions and exemptions;
* Review past DTSC decisions, correspondence, statutes, legislative analyses, regulations, rulemaking document (statement of reasons and federal registers), and any other information relevant to hazardous waste management practices for consistency in the application of regulatory and statutory interpretations;
* Develop and conduct research regarding the evaluation of hazardous waste criteria, including exclusions and exemptions, as a team member of the SB 158 Hazardous Waste Management Report and Plan project; and
* Participate in onsite visits to hazardous waste generation and treatment facilities to evaluate hazardous waste management activities in support of interpretive tasks.

**Desirable Qualifications We Look For:**
* Strong experience in written communication (memos, white papers, publications, fact sheets, FAQs, formal letters, etc.);
* Excellent oral and written skills;
* Experience researching and analyzing complex scientific and regulatory information and developing recommendations;
* Able to solve problems creatively and effectively;
* Knowledge of developing science\-based regulations and environmental policies or analyzing proposed legislation;
* An understanding of environmental regulation and/or hazardous waste management; and
* Experience in oral communication (outreach events/activities, customer interface, stakeholder meetings, presentations, etc.).

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Job Description and Duties**


The Measurement Assessment and Research Section (MARS) operates one of the Mobile Source Emissions Testing Facilities within the Mobile Source Laboratory Division (MSLD), equipped with Portable Emissions Measurement Systems (PEMS) and Portable Emissions Acquisition Systems (PEAQS) to generate high\-quality, legally defensible emissions data. MARS’s mission is to support the development and implementation of heavy\-duty on\-road and off\-road vehicle regulations, strengthen emissions inventories, inform enforcement actions, advance the Clean Truck Check program, and support innovative emissions research. Through surveillance testing of in\-use on\-road and off\-road heavy\-duty vehicles and equipment, MARS provides critical insights into real\-world emissions performance and regulatory effectiveness. MARS also serves as a platform for evaluating and demonstrating new testing approaches, developing innovative methods for measuring in\-use emissions, and expanding CARB’s testing capabilities. In collaboration with CARB mobile source workgroups, MARS develops and executes comprehensive test plans, conducts emissions testing, and performs robust data analyses to inform policy and regulatory decisions. Collectively, these efforts provide a scientific foundation for reducing criteria pollutants, greenhouse gases, and toxic air contaminants from the heavy\-duty sector and protecting public health and air quality.  

MARS is seeking an Air Pollution Specialist to perform complex technical work related to in\-use emissions characterization of heavy\-duty (HD) on\-road and off\-road vehicles and equipment. The incumbent will perform on\-road emissions measurements with portable emissions measurement systems (PEMS) and the Portable Emissions Acquisition System (PEAQS), and ensure compliance with established test procedures, data quality objectives, and safety protocols. Duties include developing and applying analytical methods for emissions data processing, validation, and interpretation; analyzing large datasets using computational tools; designing and executing test plans; operating advanced emissions measurement systems; coordinating test resources; and preparing technical reports in support of regulatory programs, research initiatives, and emissions assessments, while working independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team to support CARB’s mission to protect air quality.  

This position offers a balanced mix of laboratory, field, and office\-based work and supports CARB’s mission by advancing in\-use emissions measurement techniques and evaluating emerging heavy\-duty vehicle technologies. The incumbent's position may require Statewide travel up to 30% of the time for fieldwork, training or for meetings.
You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

*We value the time and effort you invest as you consider a career with the City of El Cerrito, and we look forward to connecting with you as we move forward in the hiring process. **What is the Role?**
The City is seeking a collaborative, enthusiastic, flexible and creative **Environmental Specialist** to join the Public Works Department!The position is based at the Recycling \+ Environmental Resource Center, which is a dynamic location that serves as a hub within the community. The Environmental Specialist performs a variety of tasks to support the City's recycling, waste reduction, and other environmental programs and operations. The incumbent will play a pivotal role in the department's functions by researching, analyzing, developing and implementing the City's programs to meet City and State environmental goals and regulatory requirements, particularly SB 1383\. In addition, this position provides technical assistance and education to residents, businesses, schools, and City staff; conducts field surveys, inspections, and data analysis; develops public outreach and educational materials; and prepares reports and recommendations. In this role, the Environmental Specialist will help support with processing grants, contracts, and other administrative tasks associated environmental program administration in the department. Furthermore, this role works with community members, regional partners, haulers, and other agencies, while also representing the City at meetings and events.  

  

The Environmental Specialist is a hands\-on position that combines community engagement, program development, fieldwork, research, and problem\-solving. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to make a direct impact on the City's environmental programs while working closely with the Operations \+ Environmental Services team. This position will report to the Senior Program Manager within the Public Works Department.

* **Vacation:** Vacation ranging from 11 to 33 days per year based on years of service.
* **Sick Leave:** Accrued at 8\.75 hours per month.
* **Tuition Reimbursement:** Cost reimbursement up to the maximum of $3,500/fiscal year for work related studies.
* **Bilingual Pay:** The City pays $2,600 per year to employees who are bilingual and who have passed a proficiency test provided by the City.

**Position Description:** 

The Academic Remediation Specialist is a licensed Registered Nurse (RN) who coordinates, delivers, monitors, and documents structured remediation and student\-success services for Vocational Nursing students with academic, clinical, skills\-competency, or professional\-conduct concerns. Working collaboratively with students, instructors, and the Director of Nursing, the Specialist supports implementation of individualized Student Success Plans, promotes safe nursing practice and student accountability, and ensures remediation activities and records align with Summit College policy and California Board of Vocational Nursing and Psychiatric Technicians (BVNPT) requirements. On site position. Regular Reliable Attendance. Teaching as needed.

**Essential Functions:**

* Receive and review instructor referrals and copies of individualized Student Success Plans for students who meet remediation criteria under the VN Remediation and Student Success Policy.
* Coordinate remediation activities and assist each referred student with implementing the interventions, responsibilities, measurable goals, expected outcomes, and timelines established in the Student Success Plan.
* Conduct remediation and student\-success meetings at the intervals defined in each plan; assess learning needs and barriers and reinforce student accountability and self\-reflection.
* Provide individualized and group tutoring, guided content review, study\-strategy coaching, learning\-style support, test\-taking strategies, and study planning for academic deficiencies.
* Support students with incomplete homework, low ATI engagement, quiz or examination scores below 80%, course averages below 78%, ATI Content Mastery scores below Level 2, or difficulty applying theoretical concepts, as referred by faculty.
* Collaborate with nursing faculty to align tutoring and remediation materials with course objectives and the BVNPT\-approved curriculum.
* Coordinate and provide skills\-lab practice, repeat skills check\-offs, faculty\-guided return demonstrations, medication\-calculation review, and simulation\-based competency reinforcement.
* Conduct structured simulation scenarios that reinforce critical thinking, clinical judgment, safe practice, communication, and technical skills in a controlled environment.

**Environmental Scientist – Contaminated Lands**

 **Environmental Scientist – Contaminated Land**


**Perth, WA \| Permanent, Full\-time**


**Who we are**


RPS, a Tetra Tech company, is a leading global professional services consultancy delivering solutions across the environment, infrastructure, energy and urban development sectors.


In Australia Asia Pacific, we work with industry, government and communities to define, design and manage complex projects that create shared value. Our people combine technical expertise with practical thinking to help clients understand environmental risks, navigate complex challenges and deliver successful project outcomes.


As part of Tetra Tech, we are connected to a global network of approximately 30,000 employees, providing access to specialist expertise, opportunities and projects across Australia and internationally.


**The Opportunity**


We are seeking a Scientist – Contaminated Land to join our Oceans \& Environment team in Perth.


This is an excellent opportunity for an early\-career environmental scientist who has some experience in contaminated land, environmental site assessment or a related area and is looking to continue developing their technical and consulting capability.


Working alongside experienced contaminated land and environmental professionals, you will contribute to a range of projects involving the investigation, assessment and management of contaminated sites.


You will have the opportunity to build your experience across field investigations, environmental sampling, data interpretation and technical reporting while learning from senior specialists with extensive experience in contaminated land assessment, remediation and environmental risk.


As your experience develops, you will be given increasing autonomy, direct client exposure and opportunities to manage smaller projects.


**What you'll be involved in**


**Your responsibilities will include:**


* Undertaking contaminated land and environmental site investigations
* Planning and participating in fieldwork, site inspections and environmental sampling programs
* Collecting, managing, analysing and interpreting environmental data
* Supporting preliminary and detailed site investigations
* Contributing to the assessment of contamination and environmental risks
* Assisting with remediation and site management projects
* Preparing clear, accurate and high\-quality technical reports and environmental advice
* Working with senior technical specialists on complex contaminated land projects
* Supporting projects involving a range of contaminants which may include hydrocarbons, heavy metals, PFAS, persistent organic pollutants and asbestos
* Liaising with laboratories, contractors, clients and other project stakeholders
* Preparing scopes of work and project costings under the guidance of senior team members
* Managing discrete or smaller projects as your capability and experience develop
* Monitoring project quality, risks, budgets and timelines
* Working collaboratively across multidisciplinary project teams
* Maintaining high standards of health, safety and environmental compliance in both field and office\-based activities


**About you**


We are looking for someone who is technically curious, practical and keen to build a career in contaminated land and environmental consulting.


**You will ideally bring:**


* A tertiary qualification in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Geology, Chemistry or another relevant discipline
* Relevant experience in contaminated land, environmental consulting, site investigation or a related field
* Experience undertaking environmental fieldwork, site investigations or sampling
* An understanding of contaminated land assessment principles and environmental data
* Strong analytical and problem\-solving skills
* Good technical report writing skills and attention to detail
* The ability to confidently work in the field as well as contribute to technical and reporting activities in the office
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills
* A collaborative approach and willingness to learn from experienced technical specialists
* The ability to work independently while knowing when to seek technical guidance
* An understanding of project delivery including quality, safety, time and budget considerations
* A commitment to ongoing professional and technical development


**Why RPS?**


Joining RPS means becoming part of a collaborative environmental team while also having access to the technical capability and opportunities of the broader Tetra Tech network.


You will have the opportunity to develop your career alongside experienced contaminated land specialists, gain exposure to a diverse range of projects and progressively take on greater technical, project and client responsibilities.


**We also offer:**


* Flexible and hybrid working arrangements where appropriate
* Professional development and career progression opportunities
* Paid professional memberships
* Active lifestyle and wellbeing initiatives
* Employee assistance and wellbeing support
* Opportunities to work with technical specialists across Australia and the wider Tetra Tech network
* A supportive and collaborative team environment
* Paid parental leave and other employee benefits


**Our commitment**


RPS is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where people are respected, supported and encouraged to bring their individual perspectives and experience to work.


If you have a foundation in environmental science or contaminated land and are looking for an opportunity to deepen your technical expertise while working alongside experienced specialists, we'd like to hear from you.

Our people live our purpose, deliver our promise, and demonstrate our behaviours every day. Our behaviours define who we are. Developed by our people, they underpin everything that we do. They create the memorable experiences we are known for and make RPS
